Kukke Subrahmaṇya
------------------------------------------
Situated between two hills—Kumāraparvata and Śeśaparvata—and very near the rivulet Kumāradhārā, Kukke Subrah-maṇya is a well-known pilgrim centre of Karnataka State. It is 105 kms. (65 miles) to the south-east of Mangalore. It was originally known as Puṣpagiri and Kukke-paṭṭaṇa (the word Kukke probably means bāla or child.).
सुब्रह्मण्य.jpg" src="http://eoh.rkmathbangalore.org/public/images/thumbs/Kukke%20Subrahma%E1%B9%87ya.jpg" alt="Kukke सुब्रह्मण्य Temple">Kukke सुब्रह्मण्य TempleIt is believed that the original shrine of सुब्रह्मण्य, the chief deity of this temple, may be at least 1500 years old.
According to the local legends, Subrahmaṇya—also known as कुमार, स्कन्द and षण्मुख (the one with six faces)—is said to have washed his weapon, the शक्ति, in the waters of the कुमार-dhārā, after killing the demon तारकासुर. Hence its name. The waters of this river is said have the power to cure skin diseases.
The chief deity of the temple complex is the six-faced सुब्रह्मण्य. Over this image is the icon of a seven hooded serpent.
In the north-east corner, there is another shrine with the images of the five deities अम्बिका (Durgā), विष्णु, गणपति, ईश्वर and सूर्य. There are also other shrines dedicated to Lakṣmīnarasiṁha and Umāmaheśvara.
There is a सुब्रह्मण्य मठ (monastery) belonging to the Mādhva tradition, the first pontiff of which was Viṣṇutīrtha (Younger brother of Madhva [ A.

-1317]).
The original deity of this temple is in a place 250 metres (820 ft.) away from the outer wall to the north. Here, there is only an anthill (with live snakes) which is worshipped as the deity सुब्रह्मण्य.
The greatest festival of this temple is the Subrahmaṇyaṣaṣṭhī usually in December.
Śaṅkara (A.
-820) is said to have visited this place.
